fr.elements: Main Residence; Detached Structure; Access Drive; Dense Vegetation; Open Terrain
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Dense Vegetation; Limited Visibility; Vegetation Near Structure
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance so responders can identify the property quickly from the road.
• Trim vegetation along both sides of the access drive to maintain a clear path wide enough for emergency vehicles.
• Cut back trees or shrubs that overhang the access drive to allow ladder trucks and taller emergency vehicles to pass without obstruction.
• Clear a turnaround area near the main residence so emergency vehicles are not forced to back out on a single-lane drive.
• Mark the access drive entrance with reflective posts if the opening is difficult to see from the road, especially at night.
• Thin dense vegetation between the road and the structures so responders approaching on foot have a visible, unobstructed path.
• Keep a clear path between the main residence and the detached structure so responders can move between the two buildings without pushing through dense growth.
• Mark or identify the detached structure with an address or unit number so responders can distinguish it from the main residence during an emergency.
• Keep any gates on the access drive unlocked or secured with a Knox Box or standard emergency lock so responders are not delayed at the entrance.
• Cut back vegetation close to both structures to give responders room to work along exterior walls without obstruction.

wildfire.conditions: Structure Surrounded by Vegetation; Tree Cluster; Tree Cluster; Tree Cluster; Scattered Trees; Vegetation Near Structure; Mixed Vegetation; Single Access Route; Long Driveway; Limited Vegetation Separation; Scattered Shrubs; Open Terrain
wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin trees closest to the house on all sides to create open space between the tree canopy and the structure.
• Remove shrubs and low-growing plants growing directly against the house walls.
• Trim the lower branches of trees near the house to raise the canopy off the ground.
• Thin out the densest tree clusters near the house to break up the concentration of trees closest to the structure.
• Separate shrubs from one another across the property so they are not touching or growing in continuous patches.
• Clear dead leaves, branches, and plant debris from the ground around the house regularly.
• Keep the driveway clear of overhanging branches along its full length to allow emergency vehicle access.
• Trim branches and shrubs along both edges of the driveway so a vehicle can pass through without obstruction.
• Remove any dead wood or fallen branches from beneath trees near the house.
• Keep grass and low ground cover mowed short in the open areas surrounding the house.
• Clear vegetation from around any outbuildings or detached structures on the property.
• Mark the driveway entrance clearly so it is easy to find quickly from the road.
